She wears a butter-yellow cotton dress with rolled short sleeves; the brief warmth of her glance toward the camera and relaxed lips give the working moment a subtle, unforced appeal. Her dark chestnut hair is gathered into one low side ponytail immediately behind her right ear. Smooth scalp strands visibly converge into that one root, and the loose tail runs continuously from the root over her right shoulder to her upper chest. On the same side, one narrow three-strand scalp braid starts at the right temple, passes above the ear, and ends inside that exact gathering. At least three alternating interwoven crossings remain clear along the braid; its terminal section visibly joins the ponytail root. A deep cobalt cloth ribbon wraps around this gathered root, tied in a compact central knot with two rounded bow loops and two short free ends. Immediately above the ribbon-wrapped root, a small polished silver crescent barrette clips into the hair, its rigid edge touching the strands and casting a narrow contact shadow. Her left hand steadies the edge of an open wooden drying press on the waist-high bench while her right hand lays the final damp botanical paper flat between its boards. Both forearms stay below the hair. A neat recovered paper stack rests beside the press; one damp sheet and a small fallen fern frond make the recent leak tangible. Wet panes and a shallow catch tray sit behind her, while late afternoon clear light enters after the rain and rakes across the braid, ribbon and silver clip. The ordinary glasshouse is quiet, still occupied by the task. The camera views her from the front-right three-quarter position, 35 degrees to her right and about 10 degrees above her eyes. Her head retains this readable angle as her eyes briefly meet the lens. Frame the whole head through below the waist in a vertical photograph, keeping the top of the head, the right temple, the gathering root and the complete hanging tail clear. A moderate portrait lens and sufficient depth of field keep face and hair connections resolved together, with the workbench readable and the farther plants softly receding. Natural skin texture, individual hair strands, damp paper edges and worn wood give the scene the specificity of an inhabited photographic moment.
